It's fun, my three year old plays with me and its like a watered down GTA. Buy houses, pets, clothes and whatnot. The only issue is the jobs are timed, the mechanics are difficult and buggy. So you have 3 minutes get across map to deliver something meanwhile the item will glitch out of your vehicle or stuck in a wall or door and you'll have to do it all over again. This is the only way to obtain money which is the main focus of the game. You get 50 to 150 dollars a job with 50 being the average. So when most items are 1000 dollars and more you can see where it gets repetitive and frustrating.

Fun, silly, and most importantly; it is something I can play with my 4 year old daughter. The amount of freedom it allows her, is perfect for anyone her age. Lots to explore and lots of secrets.

I also believe there are some valuable life lessons for children to learn from this game. For instance, it teaches the value of money and to have a work ethic. You actually have to do jobs to make money. My daughter won't stop buying things; specifically silly hats, jello, and ice cream. She then proceeds to ask why we can't go to space. I keep telling her it costs $500 to go to space. I am hoping her desire to go to space will teach her the importance of holding a steady job and not spending money like a 4 year old. She hasn't quite figured that out yet.

Honestly though, pretty great game with lots to do.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (97%): players love the co-op, with 21% of reviews praising it.
Bugs and crashes are the main complaint, though recent reviews mention them less often.

details.text: Recent reviews mention bugs and crashes less, though one says each one "costs you progress and money".
Players who have logged little time are far less positive, at 69% against 97% for those with more, so new buyers may find the early hours rougher.
